problem: The R1/R2 naming contradicts Section 3. In Section 3, R1 is the resistor from OUT to ADJ (upper) and R2 is from ADJ to ground (lower), giving Vout = 1.25(1 + R2/R1). In Section 1 the same symbols are used the other way round, so a student who carries R1 (upper) = 240 Ω and R2 (lower) = 720 Ω into Section 1's formula gets 1.25 × (1 + 240/720) = 1.67 V instead of 5 V.
fix: Use one convention throughout: Vout = Vref × (1 + R2/R1), where R2 is the resistor from OUT to the tap (upper) and R1 is from the tap to ground (lower), and state the positions explicitly in Section 1 and in Section 3.

where: Section 1 ("a temperature-stable bandgap reference of about 1.25 V")
problem: 1.25 V is the LM317's OUT-to-ADJ voltage, and the chapter presents it as the reference inside the whole three-terminal family, including the fixed 78xx/79xx, where the internal reference value is different and not a standard textbook figure. A student may then 'derive' a 7805 divider using 1.25 V.
fix: Say the chip contains "a temperature-stable internal reference" and give the 1.25 V figure only for the LM317 in Section 3. In Section 1 the divider ratio is trimmed on the die, and the part number fixes the output.

problem: "not the mirror of the 78xx order" is ambiguous — the mirror of IN–GND–OUT is OUT–GND–IN, and some books describe the 79xx as a mirrored part. A student may read the sentence as confirming a mirror.
fix: State it plainly: in TO-220 a 78xx is IN–GND–OUT; a 79xx is GND–IN–OUT, so pin 2 is the input, not the ground.
